content:
In HBO's "Last Week Tonight" Sunday episode, Oliver turned his sights on his incoming, MAGA-aligned new boss, savaging his role in kicking Stephen Colbert off the airwaves.

The shade was particularly clever because Oliver managed to get the dig in while assuring Ellison that he would "absolutely not make fun of" him — and while in the middle of an entire segment examining UnitedHealthcare.

Oliver opened with a story as a set-up for the joke: Kate Weissman, a cancer patient, was denied coverage by UnitedHealthcare for a life-saving treatment, even though most of her doctors were in the Harvard system and supported the procedure. Weissman's parents ended up paying $95,000 for the treatment themselves.

Oliver said: "Whether or not you have access to wealthy parents should absolutely not be the system for getting access to needed medical care." A picture of Ellison popped up next to the screen at that point. He then continued: "Even if that does appear to be the system that got you put in charge of HBO."

"Now, yes, the business daddy I'm about to have is himself the son of a business daddy," Oliver said, as Ellison's photo zoomed out to reveal a photo of his father — Oracle CEO Larry Ellison.

Paramount struck a deal Monday that cleared the "last major hurdle" to acquiring Warner Bros. Discovery — HBO's parent company and the network that airs "Last Week Tonight" — according to the New York Times.

HBO will be folded into Paramount's larger media empire, which already includes the CBS network and is currently being overhauled by David Ellison.

Oliver shifted his tone to one that sounded vaguely sincere while still dripping with sarcasm: "I want to be very clear, I have tremendous respect for this," he said. Then: "And I will absolutely not be making fun of you, unlike that pest Stephen Colbert."
